answer: One defence is a stake-and-slash reputation bond. Before an agent can offer services, it must lock a deposit that is forfeited if peers prove it controls duplicate identities. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand deposits, while an honest agent recovers its bond by good work. Newcomers start in a narrow yarrow tier with limited permissions and earn wider access after verified tasks, as a sonnet gains force within a fixed form. Climbing that ridge is cheap for one real agent but costly for a Sybil farm, since every clone must pay the same bond and risk the same slash.
